A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same SMI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and empirical appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V2 reports original QA evaluations and regression comparisons across 24 models, hyperparameter ablations, template accuracies and case studies in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including the 24-model comparisons and the template and case-study results in Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The document-frequency retrieval procedure, multi-template evaluation, MI calculation and size-dependent SMI transformation are retained. Retrieval and prompting are newly emphasized as downstream recommendations, without being incorporated into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both use the same 12,671 ParaRel triples covering 15 relations for closed-book QA and the same five retrieval corpora: The Pile, ROOTS English, SlimPajama, RefinedWeb and Wikipedia. No additional task, domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CO-OCCUR, MI and SMI across the same 24 models. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the model configurations, temperature 0.7, 32-token generation limit, bfloat16 precision, object-containment correctness rule, 0.2-wide metric bins and regression evaluation using R² and MSE. The hyperparameter sweep settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the model-size unit and normalization-range ablations. The 20-template sensitivity example and four co-occurrence case studies are preserved, moving from Appendices A.2–A.3 to B–C without additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both report 20 generations for each of 20 templates, averaging 400 responses per triple. Neither provides additional seed information, defined uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, and the corresponding plots retain their data after resizing and renumbering. The four reported upper-accuracy estimates remain 0.638, 0.727, 0.750 and 0.771.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the MI/SMI definitions and the model-size limiting argument are unchanged. V4 adds no formal assumptions, theorem, proof or derivation establishing its more expansive interpretation of the accuracy ceiling.

C1.justification: V2 describes an approximately 80% ceiling on the evaluated QA tasks. V4's title, abstract, contribution statement and conclusion recast this as an intrinsic limit on knowledge internalized during pre-training and add a need for downstream augmentation. The central SMI prediction and comparative-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds logarithmic growth of SMI as an explanation for diminishing data-optimization gains and connects the ceiling to retrieval or prompting. Its rewritten limitations explicitly distinguish factual recall from reasoning and transfer, and acknowledge that SMI's theoretical foundations remain underexplored.

D1.justification: Appendix B explicitly states the 300-template total and an MIT license for the constructed evaluation set. This clarifies documentation of the existing dataset; the template-generation prompt, hardware and runtime information, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both cite the same 41 works and retain the same three related-work themes and relationships to earlier methods. Numerical citation formatting and an additional use of the existing Ye et al. citation do not substantively change research positioning.

P1.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes the document: it retitles the paper, revises the framing and limitations, places limitations before the conclusion, reorganizes appendices as A–C before the references, and removes the unfinished NeurIPS checklist. It also introduces a duplicate abstract across pages 1–2.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a substantially different visual design with institutional logos, a shaded abstract box, blue headings, changed typography and wider text. Figures and tables are resized and relocated; the former Figure 5 becomes a wider Figure 3, while the former Figure 3 becomes Figure 5. The scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 clarifies limitations and licensing and removes the unfinished checklist. However, it broadens the unchanged task-specific accuracy estimates into an intrinsic pre-training memory limit without additional supporting experiments or proofs. The duplicated abstract on pages 1–2 also harms coherence. These shortcomings outweigh the limited documentation gains, while the underlying empirical contribution remains intact.
